configuration.story: A fictional campus app has one sponsored local coupon slot. Students have a short break before class; merchants want coupon redemption, not just an ad-detail click.
configuration.primary_metric: Mean per-user fraction of all eight scheduled visits with a simulated coupon redemption
configuration.feature_observability: Current intent, stated budget and minutes until class are supplied by the fictional user; merchant offer fields are known before ranking. Private preferences and outcomes are hidden from the ranker.
configuration.candidate_contract: Same eight eligible, open, valid offers for either policy; one sponsored slot; equal bids, no budget or inventory competition modeled.
configuration.clock: Accelerated simulation closes each 24-hour coupon window immediately in wall time. Coupon virtual delay and real server receipt time are separate fields; no real 24-hour wait or store visit occurs.
configuration.design: Freeze before evaluation. Same 3000 personas reused in three conditions; disjoint training/validation IDs. No tuning after outcomes.
configuration.example_rule: First B-assigned user at visit 0 whose click-policy and coupon-policy displayed offers differ in the AA and main conditions; illustrative paired simulator replay, not a new human experiment.
limits: All merchants, ads, users, clicks and redemptions are invented. Zero LLM respondent calls and zero humans.
The deliberately modeled discount-curiosity versus travel-feasibility tension is a stress-test assumption, not a discovered fact about consumers.
The models and evaluation share a simulator; conditional intervals do not measure uncertainty about actual people.
Coupon redemption is the simulated business proxy; incremental footfall, profit, revenue and auction performance are not measured.
The no-travel condition removes only the post-click travel/time constraint; budget and preference effects remain.
These models do not evaluate or replace the trained FairJob/EB-NeRD models.
